name.text: Using Trig ratios to Find the Base (copy) (copy)

questiontext.text:
A ladder of length {@LL@} metres leans against a vertical wall, making an angle of {@theta@}° with the ground.

Find the height the ladder reaches up the wall. Give your answer in exact form (no decimals).

Height reached: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We want the vertical height that the ladder reaches on the wall.

The ladder of length {@LL@} m makes an angle of {@theta@}° with the ground. This forms a right-angled triangle, where:

  • the ladder is the hypotenuse
  • the height up the wall is the opposite side

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard('jxgbox', { boundingbox: [-2, 12, 12, -2], axis: false, keepAspectRatio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false }); /* Right-angle triangle coordinates */ const A = board.create('point', [0, 0], { name: '', fixed: true, size: 2 }); // right angle const B = board.create('point', [10, 0], { name: '', fixed: true, size: 2 }); // bottom right (angle theta) const C = board.create('point', [0, 10], { name: '', fixed: true, size: 2 }); // top /* Triangle edges */ board.create('segment', [A, B]); board.create('segment', [A, C]); board.create('segment', [B, C]); /* Right-angle marker at A */ board.create('polygon', [ board.create('point', [0, 0], { visible: false }), board.create('point', [1, 0], { visible: false }), board.create('point', [1, 1], { visible: false }), board.create('point', [0, 1], { visible: false }) ], { fillColor: 'white', fillOpacity: 1, borders: { strokeColor: 'black' } }); /* Labels */ board.create('text', [5, -0.5, 'x'], { fontSize: 14 }); board.create('text', [5, 6, '{#LL#}'], { fontSize: 14 }); // hypotenuse /* Angle at B */ board.create('angle', [C, B, A], { radius: 1.2, name: '{#theta#}°', fontSize: 14, withLabel: true, strokeWidth: 2, color: 'blue' }); [[/jsxgraph]]

Using trigonometry:

height = hypotenuse × sin(angle)

So:

height = {@LL@} × sin({@theta@}°)

Using exact trigonometric values:

  • \( \sin(30°) = \frac{1}{2} \)
  • \(\displaystyle \sin(45°) = \frac{\sqrt(2)} {2} \)
  • \(\displaystyle \sin(60°) = \frac{\sqrt(3)}{2} \)

Therefore:

height = {@height@}
